subject: Post-demo: aligning on log TTL & PII carveouts
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@medsecure.com>, Rajiv Sethi <rajiv@medsecure.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: aligning on log TTL & PII carveouts

Hi Helen / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align legal & procurement: 

Summary of asks we heard from your side:
- Zero-persistence requirement for any PHI and direct customer identifiers sent to our hosted inference endpoint (you described this as "no logs retained").
- Separate minimal operational logs (token-level traces/latency) allowed for debugging if anonymized and kept only for a short TTL (you flagged 7–14 days as preferred).
- Data residency: EU region for training/request processing and backups.
- Field-level redaction/hashing option for known PII fields in prompts.
- SOC2 report + DPA language for procurement & legal review.

What we can do today (high-level):
1) Zero-data mode: ephemeral sessions only, no persistent KV or transcript storage. Extra throughput cost and a few feature tradeoffs (limited long-form state).
2) Short-log window: retain minimal operational logs (redacted) for a configurable TTL (7 / 14 / 30 days) with encryption-at-rest and strict RBAC.
3) Field-level redaction: SDK and proxy hooks to hash/strip columns before they reach the model.

Next steps proposed:
- Neha (cc) will share two contract language snippets for the carveout (zero-data and short-log).
- We’ll attach SOC2 summary and a redwood carveout template for legal review.
- If you prefer a pilot, we can scope a 30-day pilot on Short-log (7-day TTL) while legal reviews DPA for zero-data mode.

Can you confirm which approach you want us to draft into the SOW (zero-data vs 7-day short-log) and who should be on the procurement thread?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to finalize scope.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0184

From: Helen Park <helen.park@medsecure.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: aligning on log TTL & PII carveouts

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the recap. A couple clarifications from Legal/Privacy: 

- For the pilot we want ZERO persistence for PHI and for anything we identify as a customer identifier (email, account_id). That means transcripts and KV cannot be written to disk.
- For observability we are willing to accept strictly anonymized, aggregated metrics (latency, token counts) retained for up to 7 days. No request-level logs that can be tied back to a customer.
- We need field-level hashing for any free-text fields flagged by our PII scanner; hashing must be deterministic so we can still correlate but not reversible.
- Residency: EU region processing is required for production; pilot can run in US but only with explicit approval (legal@medsecure.com copied).

Attaching our internal Data Handling spec for reference. Please provide the default contract clause you’d propose for the "no-persistence" requirement.

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Park
Head of Data Privacy — MedSecure
helen.park@medsecure.com

Attachment: MedSecure_Data_Handling_Specs.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: aligning on log TTL & PII carveouts

Hi Helen / Rajiv —

Thanks for the spec, and great notes. Putting options in plain language so legal can pick: 

Option A — Zero-data mode (strict):
- No persistent transcript/KV cache. All request context is ephemeral in memory and purged on session end.
- We provide a hardened sidecar for deterministic hashing of configured fields before they reach the model.
- Operational impact: reduced ability to do long context sessions and model cache hits; expected ~8–12% extra token compute cost depending on prompt patterns.
- Contract language snippet (suggested): "Provider will not persist request transcripts or KV-store entries generated from Customer requests. Provider may collect aggregated, non-identifiable operational metrics for the purpose of service health, retained no longer than 7 days."

Option B — Short-log window (pragmatic):
- Redacted request-level logs retained for a configurable TTL (we suggest 7 days) with field-level redaction applied server-side.
- Logs encrypted-at-rest, access limited to our Infra/Legal on a need-to-know basis, audit logs tracked.
- Lower performance impact; preserves some debugging/tracing capabilities.
- Contract language snippet (suggested): "Provider will retain redacted request logs for a maximum of 7 days for operational troubleshooting. Provider will implement deterministic hashing for configured PII fields and will provide audit evidence on access."

Attachments: redwood_carveout_template.docx, SOC2_summary.pdf (high-level report).

If you choose Option A we’ll route to our engineering/policy team for a security review and produce a separate SOW for the pilot. If Option B is preferred we can draft the short-log SOW and pricing for the pilot immediately.

Proposed next steps:
- Helen: confirm preferred option (A vs B) for pilot.
- If B: we’ll send SOW + pilot quote.
- If A: we’ll provide a secure design doc and expected performance tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy & Solutions — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_carveout_template.docx; SOC2_summary.pdf

Neha — thanks for laying that out. For the pilot we want to go with Option B (Short-log window) with the following specifics: 
- TTL: 7 days for redacted request logs.
- Deterministic hashing of configured PII fields (list to be provided by our security team).
- EU-residency requirement for production; pilot can run in us-west temporarily while legal completes the DPA.

Please send the SOW and a pilot quote. Procurement is expecting a quick PO once we have the SOW and DPA. Attached is an internal PO inquiry so you can see procurement fields.

cc: legal@medsecure.com for contract intake.

Helen
